# Validation record

English | [中文](validation.zh.md)

The product goal is a complete DSH plugin. Current source includes native surfaces, appearance controls, a global workspace conversation picker, and Paper/Fabric Minecraft Host/Agent capabilities including Fabric mod discovery/install. The workspace submits operations through the selected DSH conversation; real Agent discovery, approval and server operations have not been exercised in a live DSH Profile.

The user reported that dsh-lfaa@0.1.0 installed by package name and DSH displayed a successful install; this route was not independently replayed this turn. GitHub and local-directory installs, Agent tool registration, Java discovery/download, Paper installation, and a real server start after explicit EULA acceptance remain unverified. Record each installation route and business loop separately.

This turn built `dsh-lfaa@0.1.2` and `npm pack --dry-run --json` listed the expected 14 distribution files. The local `web` Profile dependency now points to the built `0.1.2` directory. Its DSH web service was still running during the update, so the running page was not reloaded against the new package. The user-provided screenshot shows the plugin row selected with an empty central panel; the Windows browser inspection helper stopped because it could not confidently determine the current URL. Browser, Loader and real server acceptance remain pending. No test suite was run.

On 2026-10-20, the user reported that npm-name and GitHub installation both fail in DSH 0.2.1-rc.2. The npm screenshot gives the concrete cause: published `dsh-lfaa@0.1.2` requires DSH packages at `0.2.1-alpha.3`, while the installed host uses `0.2.1-rc.2`. At that point the GitHub failure details were collapsed. Source manifests and the root Git install facade were aligned with the rc.2 DSH packages, compatible Cordis/Schemastery ranges, and the client session peer/injection, advancing the package to 0.1.3. `pnpm install --lockfile-only`, offline frozen-lockfile installation, and `pnpm run build` passed. The distribution manifest has 17 peers, all DSH peers match rc.2, no prerelease peer remains, and root/distribution metadata match. `npm pack --dry-run --json` reported `dsh-lfaa@0.1.3` with the expected 14 files. `pnpm run check` was blocked by pre-existing trailing whitespace in `docs/development-master-prompt.zh.md`; no test suite or live DSH install/load was run. The user subsequently pushed this compatibility update; the latest GitHub commit visible in the supplied screenshot was `0f0763b` (`0.0.2`).

The user then pushed the GitHub install fix and confirmed that GitHub installation succeeded at `dsh-lfaa@0.1.3`. Enabling the plugin failed with `JsonSchemaError: unsupported JSON schema: parameters.properties.additionalProperties must be explicitly true or false`. The failure was reproduced against the installed `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools@0.2.1-rc.2`: the Minecraft `server.properties` map schema used a schema object for `additionalProperties`, while this DSH version requires a boolean for explicit nested objects. The schema now uses `additionalProperties: true`; the Minecraft Host owner continues to validate allowed keys, string values, and the 1–20 property limit. Focused regression (`node --test tests/minecraft-tool-schema.test.mjs`), `pnpm run build`, `npm pack --dry-run --json` (14 expected files), and `git diff --check` passed. This schema fix has not yet been pushed or retested in the user's DSH profile; update/reinstall the GitHub package before enabling it again.
